RECONSTRUCTED TEXT — Open Library search-inside, 2026-09-06
===========================================================
GUIDE PETIT FUTÉ — CITY GUIDE MONTRÉAL, ÉDITION 2011-2012 (Le Petit Futé, ISBN 9782746930636)
Internet Archive: guidepetitfuteci0000coll — scan leaf 342; the guide's own index gives page 236.

NOT A SCAN. The book is lending-restricted and has not been read. The entry below was assembled
from twenty-eight overlapping twelve-word windows returned by
https://openlibrary.org/search/inside.json (contract at f_4933). Page images return HTTP 403.


THE ENTRY, walked forward from the heading
------------------------------------------

    "CAMP Y KANAWANA
    514-849-5331
    www.ymcakanawana.ca

    Premier camp de vacances au Québec, situé à Saint-Sauveur, et membre fondateur de
    l'Association des camps du Québec, celui-ci propose des programmes de camp d'été résidentiels
    de 6 à 12 jours aux jeunes de 7 à 16 ans, ainsi que des programmes de leadership et d'aventures
    en plein air aux campeurs de 11 à 20 ans. En opération du 28 juin au 20 août, le camp Y
    Kanawana organise des séjours de six jours à huit semaines. Selon leurs intérêts, les jeunes
    ont accès à des activités de baignade, canot, kayak, trampoline aquatique, tir à l'arc,
    escalade, hébertisme, cours de survie en plein air, danse, école du rock, théâtre, etc. Les
    jeunes participent également à des ateliers de sciences naturelles ou à des activités comme
    La faune gagne du terrain qui permet de les conscientiser à la biodiversité. Cette année, les
    mordus de rafting et de kayak âgés de 13 à 16 ans pourront profiter au maximum du tout nouveau
    programme Aventurier Extrême, leur permettant de faire du rafting et du kayak en eau vive, de
    l'escalade sur roche, ainsi qu'un parcours dans les arbres. Pour les autres, tout aussi
    téméraires, le camp propose des expéditions de canot-camping inoubliables! Les activités
    Explorateurs (11 et 12 ans) et Aventuriers (13 à 16 ans) proposent en effet aux jeunes de vivre
    une excursion de quatre jours, ..."

THE WALK STOPS THERE, mid-sentence. "Une excursion de quatre jours" returns thirty-three hits
across the corpus — a French guidebook commonplace — and no longer isolates this book. The tail of
the entry is unrecovered. Accents and apostrophes have been restored from the OCR ("intéréts",
"tir a Varc", "13 416 ans", "13 8 16 ans", "|'Association"); the words are the book's.


WHAT IS NEW HERE
----------------
- A SEASON: 28 June to 20 August.
- A STAY RANGE: six days to eight weeks, with residential programmes of 6-12 days for ages 7-16
  and leadership and outdoor-adventure programmes for 11-20.
- ACTIVITIES this project does not hold: **trampoline aquatique**, **école du rock**, **danse**,
  **théâtre**, and **cours de survie en plein air**.
- A NAMED BIODIVERSITY ACTIVITY: **"La faune gagne du terrain"**, described as consciousness-raising
  about biodiversity — which belongs with the environmental-education material and is not in it.
- **AVENTURIER EXTRÊME**, called "tout nouveau" in this edition: whitewater rafting and kayaking,
  rock climbing and a tree-top course, for 13-16s. **"Cette année" dates its introduction to 2011
  or 2012**, and this is the only date this project has for it.
- The **Explorateurs (11-12)** and **Aventuriers (13-16)** tiers, each running a four-day excursion.


TWO CLAIMS THAT ARE THE GUIDE'S, NOT FINDINGS
---------------------------------------------
**"Premier camp de vacances au Québec."** A primacy claim in a commercial tourist guide, whose
entry reads throughout like copy the camp supplied. `canadian-camping-movement.md` has spent three
revisions taking an ordinal ranking out of this wiki, because Big Cove and Camp Stephens both put
dates in front of 1894. One more repetition of the camp's own line does not put it back.

**"Membre fondateur de l'Association des camps du Québec."** This is new here and it is not
verified. This project holds the Quebec association's English Section as founded in **1937** and
holds **no membership roll for that year**. Whether Kanawana was among the founders is therefore an
open question — and, unlike the primacy claim, a **checkable** one: the ACQ's own records, or the
English Section's minutes for 1937-49, would settle it. Recorded as a question, not an answer.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, which is the point worth keeping. This item is on p_430's group 6 list, described
there as "the Petit Futé Montreal city guide 2011-12" among items that "may simply cite the camp as
an example". It does nothing of the kind — it carries the longest French-language description of
Kanawana's programme this project holds. It surfaced not from the worklist but from a query run for
a completely different purpose: **"Kanawana" "Westbury"**, run to fix a telephone number in the 1991
ski guide. A worklist entry written from a catalogue title underestimated it, and a control query
for another book found what was in it.
